newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Taiwan's CPC Taoyuan crude pipeline damaged again.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan's CPC Taoyuan crude pipeline damaged again.

text.p: Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp has again shut down an oil pipeline at its Taoyuan refinery following a damage incurred during crude discharge early Wednesday, a source at the refinery said.
The source said that as a result of the unexpected delay to crude discharge, the refinery would not be able to restart a second 100,000-barrel-per-day (bpd) unit for at least another five days.
The crude unit was due to restart later this week once CPC successfully discharges its crude feedstock, the source said. The unit has been down since September 14-15.
"We will only restart the second crude unit when we have 30 days of crude oil supply for both units in our tanks," the source said. CPC's other crude unit also has a 100,000-bpd capacity.
The official said there are two other tankers carrying a total of 500,000-tonnes of crude oil waiting outside its refinery waiting to discharge.
A third tanker, the Vanadis, had only managed to discharge 200,000 tonnes of its 300,000 tonnes crude cargo.
The Taoyuan refinery presently has stocks of about 370,000 tonne, enough to run just one crude unit for about 25 days, the official said.
Repair works on the latest damage to the pipeline would take at least one day, he said.
The Taoyuan refinery closed both its crude oil pipelines during mid-September due to oil leaks. Repair works on the second line were expected to be completed much later.
Last week CPC said it aimed to reopen one crude discharge line sometime this week.
The unexpectedly long shutdown of the pipeline and consequently the crude unit, forced CPC to double its jet fuel purchases.
In its October jet fuel import tender, CPC bought two 32,000-tonne cargoes at $244.80 and $247.82 per tonne on a cost-and-freight basis to Keelung or Shen Ao.
The Taoyuan refinery produces 60,000 tonnes of jet fuel a month at full capacity.
